newsitem.title: USA: Milwaukee stadium bill in trouble in Wis. Senate.
newsitem.headline: Milwaukee stadium bill in trouble in Wis. Senate.

text.p: Questions of legality sent a bill that would cap the use of local sales tax revenues for a $250 million ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team to an "unfriendly" Wisconsin Senate committee Tuesday.
The bill, which passed the Senate Economic Development, Housing and Government Operations Committee on Monday, was pending before the full Senate Tuesday for a vote.

However, lawmakers voted 18 to 15 to send the bill to the Senate Judiciary Committee because of legal questions that arose, according to a spokeswoman for State Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona, the bill's chief sponsor.
The spokeswoman said that committee is headed by State Sen. Lynn Adelman, D-New Berlin, who will likely seek to let the bill die there.

Wineke's bill, which he introduced earlier this month, would set a $160 million bond limit for the stadium's state-created oversight and development agency, the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District.
The district on March 5 sold $146.7 million of tax-exempt, sales tax revenue bonds backed by a 0.1 percent, five-county sales tax and insured by MBIA Insurance Corp.
The bill would also prohibit any of the sales tax revenues from being used to make lease payments for stadium costs.
District officials have condemned the bill as being unconstitutional and likely to kill the project if passed.
